verdicts.evidence: - [H] Climbing costs 1 extra foot per foot (2 in Difficult Terrain).
verdicts.rule_quote: Difficult Terrain isn’t cumulative; either a space is Difficult Terrain or it isn’t.
verdicts.explanation: The scenario adds climbing's extra foot and Difficult Terrain's extra foot (3 ft per foot). That is Reading A of 'not cumulative' (only Difficult Terrain sources don't stack). Reading B would give 2 ft per foot.

verdicts.explanation: 5 ft of climbing in Difficult Terrain costs 15 ft, so the climb extra and the Difficult Terrain extra stack. That assumes Reading A. Under Reading B it would cost 10. The test does check that Difficult Terrain adds exactly 1 extra foot per foot on top of the climb cost.

summary: The engine only has a coarse Difficult Terrain flag: a per-move `difficult` argument and a scene-wide `scene.difficult`. Together they add 1 extra foot per foot once. Clauses #5–#10 (creature, furniture, liquid, narrow opening, slope) have no implementation or SRD tests. Neither scenario test checks the 1-extra-foot rule directly. The EXPL-04 test is the only one that checks the cost, and it relies on one reading of 'not cumulative'. The nine page-181 code candidates (Dodge, exhaustion, dehydration and similar) are about other rules, so I gave them no verdict.
